required_for: queue depth/status when broker state is needed
optional_or_degraded_for: isolated backend mode without broker-backed ingestion
extraction activity signaling when file fallback is available

evidence.finding: Compose defines Redis and makes backend/worker/gpu_worker/beat depend on Redis service start.
Settings define and normalize redis_url, celery_broker_url, and celery_result_backend for host vs Docker runtime.
Celery broker/result backend use Redis-derived settings and configure specialized queues.
Redis is used for queue depths and extraction/GPU-exclusive activity; file fallback exists when Redis is unavailable.
Backend probes Redis connectivity and reports queue status from Redis LLEN.
Cockpit health and queue endpoints probe Redis and queue depths.
Worker contract documents Redis as Celery broker/result backend and queue-depth probe source.
Runtime docs list Redis port 6379 as Celery broker/result backend and say to start it when running Celery mode.
Environment check requires Redis/Celery broker only when task_mode is not sync.

risks_and_gaps.item: Docs and health surfaces should distinguish Redis-down in Celery mode from Redis-down in sync mode.
Queue status depends on Redis reachability and should not be interpreted as canonical task history.
Broker-backed ingestion is unavailable when TASK_MODE=celery and Redis is unreachable.
Live Redis process status was not sampled in this audit.

scope: status/health copy or docs only if separately approved
